item.title: What Does It Actually Mean to Write ‘Like a Human’?
item.description:
<![CDATA[
What does it mean to write with a “human touch”? That’s what Marcus Olang’, a writer in Nairobi, Kenya, wondered after he was told a project proposal he worked on for days sounded as if it was written by ChatGPT. He explains how the massive effort to crack down on A.I. writing hides a deeper story. It’s not actually about technology, but how fluid and fraught the definition of sounding — being — human has always been.

item.title: Notable Books
item.description:
Good morning! Want to add a new book to your 2026 reading list? It’s not too late.

Our list of the 100 most notable books of the year just dropped, and I’m eager to get reading. I’ve been slacking this year (mainly because I’ve been reading a lot of news), but I did finish “Yesteryear” by Caro Claire Burke.

Not sure where to start? Use our guide. The categories will help you match the vibe you’re looking for. I’m going to read “Lost Lambs” by Madeline Cash next, which my friend Morgan lent to me. What books have you loved this year? Tell me.

We’re also covering:

Jensen Huang

The new Labubu?

Thanksgiving tips

What to discuss in class today.

1. President Trump pushed for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as chief executive of Nvidia. Trump set in motion a weekend of maneuvering, led by Vice President JD Vance, to get Huang his job back. Here’s how he did it.

2. The Army is moving ahead with plans to blow up a stockpile of explosives in Iowa tomorrow. It threatens to send a cloud of toxic lead dust over homes and farmland.

3. Representative Jimmy Gomez of California said that he would resign from Congress. A House committee had found that he had engaged in “unwelcome sexual conduct” with a female congressional aide.

4. More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to a new estimate from hacked government data.

5. Some Haitian families fleeing to Canada are being separated at the border. Many are being denied entry, turned back and detained by U.S. authorities.

6. What’s in those drugs at gas station convenience stores and smoke shops? We tested some to find out.

What you’re wearing.

Cindy Phan, 20, neuroscience major at the University of Alabama

The outfit: My friends and I celebrated the upcoming release of “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” by having a “Hunger Games”-themed Friendsgiving costume party! My outfit is roughly based on Effie Trinket’s monarch butterfly look (on a budget and rushed time frame). It was an absolute blast. Don’t forget, “eyes bright, chins up, smiles on!”

Tell me more! I love hosting hangouts with my friends, and having a themed party is my absolute favorite. I think college students should bring back embracing our inner child and live a life full of whimsy, not caring what other people think. There are more ways to have fun in college than just going out to the bars!

Submit your outfits to Fit Check.

I’m now obsessed with Ralphie VII, the University of Colorado’s live buffalo mascot. The previous Ralphie, known as Ralphie VI, retired because of her “indifference to running.”

The Make America Great Again movement wants to remake Harvard. Now Harvard has a class for that. See what was on the syllabus.

Walter Willett, a nutritionist at Harvard, studies the link between diet and health, which is a high priority for Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. His grants were frozen anyway.

A freshman at Stanford University was arrested after allegedly hacking into on-campus businesses and stealing funds. (The Stanford Daily)

The University of Minnesota announced its plan to close six residential communities designed to serve specific cultural groups in its dorms. Four of the communities were under scrutiny from the federal government. (The Minnesota Daily)

The new Labubu? Meet the Mirumi. The robotic bag charm can grab onto your bag and turn its head at the sound of your voice. My colleague Alisha Haridasani Gupta, who wrote this story, showed me the Mirumi in the newsroom. I need one.

Would you bid on live lobsters? It’s possible on Whatnot, a livestream auction app that is a cross between eBay and Twitch. You can also buy king crab legs, Wagyu hot dogs and ground beef.

Miley Cyrus got married. She married her partner of several years, Maxx Morando, at Frank Sinatra’s estate in Palm Springs, Calif.

Do these to get ahead for Thanksgiving!

Eat for pleasure. Savoring food for pleasure isn’t exclusively for the holidays. It may have long-term benefits.

Travel smart (and safe). If the recent outages have made you nervous, consult our Thanksgiving travel guide.

Looking for more things to read en route? Peruse some Thanksgiving-themed literature.

Don’t go to the emergency room. Avoid Thanksgiving hazards with these tips. Please, please don’t deep-fry a frozen turkey!

We want to know what you talk about at the Thanksgiving table. Tell us all about it here.

Thanks for hanging out with me this morning. We’re taking the rest of the week off for the holiday. We’ll see you Monday!

This newsletter is powered by your submissions — tell us about your classes, questions, crushes, side hustles and obsessions here.

Also: Times access is free for half of all U.S. college students through their school. Tell your friends to check if their school provides free access.

Forward this to your roommate, professor, club president or T.A.

Want more of today’s top stories? Tune in to “The Headlines,” our podcast that includes top headlines and analysis.

Any tips or feedback? I’m all ears. Email me at extracredit@nytimes.com.

The editor of Extra Credit is Talya Minsberg. Philip Pacheco and Hiroko Masuike were our photo editors.
